exposure: Type of anesthesia during delivery (general anesthesia vs. spinal anesthesia)
outcome: Neonatal otoacoustic emission (OAE) hearing test results
cohort: 1,493 healthy, full-term (39/0-40/6 gestational weeks) newborns of healthy women delivered by cesarean section
finding: Newborns delivered via cesarean section with general anesthesia had a significantly higher rate of false-positive results on OAE hearing tests compared to those delivered with spinal anesthesia.
mod_finding: Neonates delivered by cesarean section with general anesthesia had a statistically significant higher rate of false-positive results on otoacoustic emission hearing tests compared to those delivered with spinal anesthesia.
